title: Fear Wins and a Generation Waits
overview: Frightened by the scouts' report, the Israelites refuse to enter the land God promised, and that whole adult generation is told it will die in the wilderness while their children inherit the land.

parts.label: The people want to turn back (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: After the scouts' report of powerful enemies, the people weep all night and accuse God of bringing them out only to be killed. They even talk of choosing a new leader to take them back to Egypt, where they had been slaves.

parts.label: Four men face the crowd (vv. 5-10)
parts.note: Moses and Aaron fall facedown, though the text does not say whether they are appealing to the people or to God, while Joshua and Caleb tear their clothes in grief and insist the land is good and its people's protection (literally their 'shadow') is gone. The crowd talks of stoning them until the LORD's glory appears at the tent of meeting, the sacred tent where God met with Moses.

parts.label: Moses argues for the people (vv. 11-19)
parts.note: God threatens to destroy them and build a new nation from Moses, but Moses argues the other nations would say God could not finish what he started. He then appeals to God's own description of himself as slow to anger and rich in love, and asks for forgiveness.

parts.label: Forgiven, but not let in (vv. 20-25)
parts.note: God forgives, which here seems to mean the nation will not be wiped out, yet those who saw his signs and still tested him 'ten times' (probably meaning again and again) will not enter the land. Caleb is singled out for following wholeheartedly, and the people are told to turn back toward the desert.

parts.label: Forty years in the wilderness (vv. 26-38)
parts.note: In a grim echo of their own complaint, everyone counted in the census aged twenty and up who grumbled will die in the wilderness, one year for each day of scouting, while the children they feared would be captured receive the land. Only Joshua and Caleb are spared, and the ten scouts who spread the bad report die in a plague.

parts.label: A failed attack (vv. 39-45)
parts.note: Grieving, the people now try to invade on their own, but Moses warns that the LORD is not with them, and neither he nor the ark (the sacred chest representing God's presence) leaves camp. The Amalekites and Canaanites of the hill country beat them back as far as Hormah.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether God truly changed his plan in response to Moses' prayer, or whether the threat to destroy the people was meant all along to draw out that prayer.
think: When fear and hope pull you in opposite directions, what helps you tell which one is seeing the situation more clearly?
